notes.Tower: P85: All 11 Tower orchestration tools (TowerInit, TowerPlan, TowerSpawn, TowerMerge, TowerTeardown, TowerSend, TowerInbox, TowerFinding, TowerReview, TowerMission, TowerStatus) execute natively via the Git and .tower/ protocol.
notes.WaitFor: P82: v2's task-wait tool (WaitFor) executes natively via the state bridge (domain: 'task', action: 'wait').
notes.AgentSwarm: P82: v2's AgentRunBatch executes natively (swarm_tool.rs). Resume is gated on ownership: a member may only be resumed by the agent that spawned it, and the two v2 refusals are kept apart ('is not a subagent' for an id the engine never spawned, 'does not belong to this parent agent' for someone else's), enforced in the swarm launcher's resume (swarm/service.rs require_ownedSubagent) against the parent recorded at spawn. A resumed member keeps the swarm item it was spawned for (v2 getSwarmItem). fork runs v2's forkIncompatibility gate, the one the single-agent Agent tool already ran: a fork shares the caller's profile and model, so a differing subagent_type/model, or any non-empty resume_agent_ids, is refused. One intentional divergence from v2: empty strings in items / resume_agent_ids are filtered out before the >=2 count check, so a list of one real item plus one empty string is rejected here as a single item where v2's zod schema would have rejected the empty string first; the native behaviour is the stricter, intended one.
notes.TaskWait: REPL-only def (task_tools.rs:611). No v2 product tool is named TaskWait — v2's task-wait tool is WaitFor (host-owned).
notes.list_directory: Executable natively (tools/mod.rs execute()) and now advertised: `list_directory_tool_def()` is pushed by `all_native_tool_defs()`, which is what `GET /api/v1/tools` reports as active builtins. Before that it was advertised by no tool def anywhere — not even build_repl_tool_defs — so the capability existed but the model could never call it. G-8's 'REPL 可达' was wrong; corrected here, and the advertised-set invariant is now asserted by `core_tool_defs::tests::advertised_native_tools_are_executable`.
notes.Agent: P46 (2026-09-02): the foreground core of v2's Agent tool (agentTool.ts) executes natively — the host pushes the session's profile catalog per turn and the engine runs the subagent through the same native pipeline. Routing is conditional: resume / fork / background / model args, profiles missing from the snapshot (plugin sources, external backends) and runtime-less transports fall back to the host tool, which stays registered. Pre-P46 this entry read 'host-owned, invoke_subagent family REPL-only' (G-8).
notes.ReadMediaFile: Not a registered tool anymore — Read handles media internally (readTool.ts:308 via execute-media-read). The name survives only in permission lists (matchesRule.ts:82, default-tool-approve.ts:9) and TUI renderers. G-8 listed it as a v2 registered name; corrected here.
notes.Knowledge: Fork-original (ROADMAP records the layout as a fork convention): upstream v2 at 21406fb4c8 has no knowledge-tool.ts and no knowledge feature at all — a tree-wide search for `*knowledge*` under agent-core-v2 returns nothing. An earlier version of this entry cited an 'agent/knowledge/tools/knowledge-tool.ts that self-registers but is imported by nothing'; that path existed only in THIS FORK's retired v2 copy. The tool originates from the retired kimi-native-tools crate. Native twins exist in BOTH places: the REPL (repl/mod.rs knowledge_tool_def) and the host-driven session table (tool_policy::native_tool_defs pushes knowledge_tool_def), with an execution arm in tools/mod.rs.
notes.Team: Fork-original, like Knowledge: upstream v2 at 21406fb4c8 has no teamTool.ts, no Team tool and no debate machinery — a tree-wide search for `*team*` under agent-core-v2 returns nothing. The earlier 'teamTool.ts self-registers but is imported by nothing' described this fork's retired v2 copy. Native twins exist in BOTH the REPL (repl/mod.rs team_tool_def) and the host-driven session table (tool_policy::native_tool_defs), with an execution arm in tools/mod.rs. ROADMAP 139 and the matrix row at 1249-1250 already record Team as a fork feature; this entry now agrees with them.
notes.run_code: Fork-original and never wired on either side: upstream v2 at 21406fb4c8 has no codeRuntime feature (a tree-wide search for `*codeRuntime*` / `*runCode*` returns nothing), and the fork's own retired v2 copy had a 'codeRuntimeFeature imported by no module'. No native arm, no REPL def. batch4 assessment treated it as a live v2 tool to evaluate; corrected here.
notes.lsp: Fork-original, with no v2 counterpart at all: at upstream HEAD (21406fb4c8) a tree-wide search for `*lsp*` under agent-core-v2 returns nothing, and agent/toolPolicy/evaluate.ts has no LSP entry. An earlier version of this entry described a 'v2 side' whose 'lspFeature is imported by no feature assembly' — that described this fork's own retired v2 copy, not upstream. Rust side: there IS a native arm (tools/mod.rs "lsp" => lsp_tool::execute_lsp_tool) and a def (core_tool_defs.rs lsp_tool_def, pushed by all_native_tool_defs), so it is advertised by `GET /api/v1/tools` as an active builtin. The name was missing from NATIVE_TOOL_NAMES, which made handles() false and forwarded every call to a host with no tool runtime — the call could only fail. It is now in NATIVE_TOOL_NAMES, so the advertisement is truthful; it deliberately stays out of the host-driven session table (native_tool_defs), which is what tool_policy's `!names.contains("Lsp")` assertion pins. ROADMAP 6.39 records the provenance.
notes.Memory: Fork-original: upstream v2 at 21406fb4c8 registers no memory_* tool (a tree-wide search for those names returns nothing); the six tools execute natively against the memory filesystem under `~/.kimi-code/memory/` (tools/memory_store.rs + tools/memory_tool.rs). The def names are the snake spellings the memory section documents, so the squashed twins are the aliases here. Unlike Lsp they ARE in the host-driven session table (tool_policy::native_tool_defs): the memory section ships in the default system prompt (SystemPromptBuilder::build_default* enables it), so the tools and the section are advertised together.
notes.session_query: Fork-original and never wired on either side: upstream v2 at 21406fb4c8 has no sessionQuery feature (a tree-wide search for `*sessionQuery*` returns nothing). No native arm, no REPL def.
notes.unloadedInV2: M3a (2026-09-01) deleted the unloaded tool features (lsp / sessionQuery / codeRuntime / knowledge / team / workflow / memory / attachment) from THIS FORK's agent-core-v2 copy. The earlier wording — 'deleted from agent-core-v2 entirely' — conflated two cases and has been corrected against upstream HEAD (21406fb4c8) by tree-wide search: (a) fork-original, never upstream — lsp, workflow, sessionQuery, codeRuntime, knowledge, team, and the six memory_* tools all return zero hits under agent-core-v2/src; (b) genuinely removed from the fork's copy while still living upstream — 'attachment' is a live v2 concept (human/agent/origin.ts PromptFileAttachment, agent/media attachmentStore, agent/tools/fileReadSource.ts attachmentFileSource), so M3a removed the fork's copy of something upstream still has. 'Deleted from agent-core-v2' is therefore accurate only for (b). The section is kept empty so a re-wired tool fails the TS unclassified check instead of silently passing. ROADMAP 6.39 records the split.
notes.mcp: MCP runtime-discovered tools are host-owned by design: handles() never matches them, so they round-trip to the host's MCP runtime. The engine's own McpManager serves them only in REPL standalone mode (execute_tool's fallback arm).
notes.github: GitHub tool names are a dynamic family matched by github::is_github_tool against its SPECS table, not part of NATIVE_TOOL_NAMES. v2Github pins the v2 registration set to the engine's SPECS — a tool added on one side fails the other side's test.
notes.aliases: The snake spellings are load-bearing: subagent/manager.rs allowlists, permission/mod.rs and repl/mod.rs match them. Do not prune without sweeping those call sites.
notes.scope: The v2 side of this contract is enumerated from the real tool registry (features assembled with every experimental flag on, then IAgentToolRegistryService.list()) — not a hand-maintained list. Tools registered by the app layer outside agent-core-v2 are host-owned by construction: handles() rejects any name not in NATIVE_TOOL_NAMES.
notes.replOnlyNativeGroup: The group label is historical: these are engine-native names that are NOT part of the v2-registered tool surface. Knowledge/Team/select_tools/list_directory/... are advertised by the host-driven session table or the REPL; `lsp` is advertised only by `all_native_tool_defs()` (i.e. `GET /api/v1/tools`), and the six memory tools by both that surface and the session table. All of them execute natively when a host asks for them. `is_native_tool_name` accepts every name in this group (asserted by tools::tests::native_tool_names_match_the_contract_file), which is the property the group actually pins.
